From: Andrew Chen <andrew@finpay.com>

Subject: VPC connectivity integration - discovery follow-up

Thanks Marissa and team — great call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can prioritize internally:

Summary of requirements (from today's discovery):
- Private connectivity: we need VPC endpoint support so requests to Redwood never traverse the public internet.
- IP allowlist / static egress: we need a predictable set of IPs for firewall rules and an option to restrict inbound to Redwood endpoints to those IPs.
- Egress/dns: outbound DNS resolution from our VPC must resolve Redwood endpoints; if there are requirements for specific DNS zones or split-horizon config please call out.
- mTLS: mutual TLS for service-to-service auth is preferred for high-sensitivity routes.
- Auth: we plan to use service-account tokens for API calls; please confirm supported auth methods for VPC endpoints and SDK flows.
- SDK & integration: we will embed the SDK into our backend; want to confirm support for structured output/tool-calling and embedding/recall (embeddings + reranker flow).

Next steps from FinPay:
- I'll loop in our Network Ops (cc'ed) and schedule a technical deep-dive for our infra team.
- We can share our subnet and firewall admin contact in advance.

Please send a one-page onboarding checklist and any architecture diagrams/prereqs (CSR for mTLS, IP ranges, recommended DNS config).

Thanks,
Andrew Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
FinPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: VPC connectivity integration - discovery follow-up

Thanks Andrew — appreciate the clear recap. Short note to confirm what we discussed and propose concrete next steps.

Recap / what Redwood can provide:
- VPC endpoints: Redwood supports private connectivity via managed VPC endpoints (we call them Private Connect endpoints) that allow your VPC to reach Redwood services without public egress.
- IP allowlist / static egress: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can provide fixed egress IPs for firewall rules. For hosted/shared tiers we provide NATed egress ranges; we can confirm the exact CIDR blocks for your region.
- DNS: We recommend adding a zone delegation or private hosted zone that resolves Redwood endpoint hostnames. If you need split-horizon, we'll provide the service names you should map.
- mTLS: Supported. We can do client-auth with mutual TLS for service-to-service traffic to the Private Connect endpoint. We support customer-supplied certs and automated rotation via KMS/HSM integrations.
- Auth & SDK: Primary auth for VPC endpoints is bearer tokens (service account tokens). Our official SDK supports retrieving tokens (OIDC/service account) and automatic retry/routing logic for private endpoints. Structured output/tool-calling and embeddings are supported end-to-end — embeddings are stored in a managed vector store for routing/reranking; reranker pipelines are available via our SDK and REST API.

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline):
- Marissa (me): share onboarding checklist + high-level architecture diagram (attached) and a proposed mutual action plan by EOD today. [attachment: vpc-quickstart.pdf]
- Lauren: technical deep-dive on networking, IP ranges, DNS, and mTLS config — propose Tue 2026-08-11 10:00 PST.
- Jonas: go over SDK integration, auth flows, and embedding/reranker guidance in the deep-dive.

Action items for FinPay:
- Share subnets, firewall admin contact, and preferred deep-dive attendees.
- If you have constraints on certificate authorities for mTLS please include those.

If that works I’ll lock the calendar and send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Chen <andrew@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity integration - discovery follow-up (technical clarifications)

Hi Andrew — quick technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive:

1) VPC Endpoints and DNS
- For Private Connect we provision endpoint network appliances in your VPC (either an AWS PrivateLink-style endpoint or our managed proxy inside your VPC on Dedicated). You can either delegate a private hosted zone to our endpoint or add explicit A/AAAA records for the hostnames we provide.
- If you use split-horizon DNS, ensure your VPC resolver can resolve the delegated zone. We will provide the hostnames: "privateapi.us.redwood.internal" and per-region variants.

2) IP allowlist / static egress
- For Dedicated customers we can give you a small set (4-8) of static egress IPs you can rely on for outbound requests (for example, callbacks or health checks). For Hosted customers we publish a range per region (these are NATed and may change with advance notice).

3) Egress / DNS for embeddings & reranker calls
- Embedding ingestion and reranker scoring are internal services exposed via the same Private Connect endpoint. No additional public egress is required if you use the Private Connect path. If you plan to host your own vector DB, we can provide an egress path for vector exchange, but that requires an explicit allowlist and routing config.

4) mTLS and cert rotation
- We support client-auth mTLS. Two common patterns:
  - Customer-supplied certs: you provide a CA-signed client certificate (and rotation plan).
  - Managed certs: we can generate/rotate certs and store keys in your KMS/HSM; short-lived cert distribution happens over the private control channel.
- Please confirm which pattern you prefer; if customer-supplied, include CSR/CA details before the deep-dive.

5) SDK/auth and structured output
- Our SDK supports:
  - Service-account token exchange (OIDC flow) with optional short-lived tokens for calls over the Private Connect.
  - Automatic routing to the Private Connect endpoint when a tenancy flag is set.
  - Structured output parsing helpers and tool-calling scaffolding (we can share a sample integration where agents call an internal tool and return structured JSON).
- For embeddings/rerankers: we recommend batching ingestion and using our incremental upsert API. Reranker calls should include references to embedding ids; we can share a sample sequence in the deep-dive.

Proposed slot: Tue 2026-08-11 10:00 PST — I’ll send an invite once you confirm attendees.

Attachment: config-sample.yaml (text/plain)

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Principal Solution Architect, Network & Security
Redwood Inference
